lines.trans: Look at Javier's cutting board, Rocio: every carrot cube is identical!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: Even cubes cook at the exact same speed, brother. Basic physics!
Laugh all you want, Tomas, those are the neatest chopped vegetables in my kitchen!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: The pot is warm with olive oil: do I put the onion and carrot in now?
Yes! Stir three minutes until golden, and then add red lentils and hot broth.
Do you need the courtyard thyme and parsley next, boss?
Two fresh little sprigs tied with string, and one pinch of salt at the end.
Hearing soup simmer in a stone kitchen beats city traffic any day.
Funny: three years ago we argued on the phone, and today we make soup together.
Remind me never to wait three years to call you again, Tomas.
All right, brothers, save the tears because the bread timer is ringing!
Oven mitts on! Eight freshly baked crusty loaves coming out hot!
Look at Javier's cutting board, Rocio: every carrot cube is identical!

Laugh all you want, Tomas, those are the neatest chopped vegetables in my kitchen!

Yes! Stir three minutes until golden, and then add red lentils and hot broth.
Do you need the courtyard thyme and parsley next, boss?

Remind me never to wait three years to call you again, Tomas.
All right, brothers, save the tears because the bread timer is ringing!
Oven mitts on! Eight freshly baked crusty loaves coming out hot!
Look at Javier's cutting board, Rocio: every carrot cube is identical!

Laugh all you want, Tomas, those are the neatest chopped vegetables in my kitchen!

Yes! Stir three minutes until golden, and then add red lentils and hot broth.
Do you need the courtyard thyme and parsley next, boss?
Two fresh little sprigs tied with string, and one pinch of salt at the end.
Hearing soup simmer in a stone kitchen beats city traffic any day.
Funny: three years ago we argued on the phone, and today we make soup together.
Remind me never to wait three years to call you again, Tomas.
All right, brothers, save the tears because the bread timer is ringing!
Oven mitts on! Eight freshly baked crusty loaves coming out hot!
See you!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Used both for cooking oil (aceite de oliva) and lubricating oil on hinges.

examples.text: Pon dos gotas de aceite en la bisagra seca.
examples.trans: Put two drops of oil on the dry hinge.

examples.text: Aliñamos la sopa caliente con aceite de oliva.
examples.trans: We dress the hot soup with olive oil.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.text: Voy para allá ahora mismo.
examples.trans: I am heading there right now.

examples.text: Ahora tenemos cuatro mesas libres.
examples.trans: Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from atar (to tie).

examples.text: Es una pieza atada.
examples.trans: It is a tied piece.

examples.text: Hay una pequeña tarjeta de cartón atada al asa.
examples.trans: There is a small cardboard card tied to the handle.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb; everyday cooking word for adding ingredients to a pot or bowl (añade el caldo).

examples.text: Añade una pizca de sal y dos hojas de laurel a la sopa.
examples.trans: Add a pinch of salt and two bay leaves to the soup.

examples.text: Añadimos zumo de limón fresco a la crema templada.
examples.trans: We added fresh lemon juice to the warm cream.

meanings.note: Tener ... años expresses age; hace ... años means '... years ago'.

examples.text: El año está aquí.
examples.trans: The year is here.

examples.text: Vemos los años desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the years from the door.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.text: ¡Buenos días a todos!
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!

examples.text: Hace muy buen tiempo hoy.
examples.trans: The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Antepenultimate stress (esdrújula) keeps its written accent across all four forms.

examples.text: Harina, agua, sal y levadura son los ingredientes básicos del pan.
examples.trans: Flour, water, salt, and yeast are the basic ingredients of bread.

examples.text: Es una regla básica de física y de buena cocina.
examples.trans: It is a basic rule of physics and good cooking.

meanings.note: Invariable before masculine or feminine singular nouns (cada día, cada mañana).

examples.text: Abro la cafetería cada mañana.
examples.trans: I open the cafe every morning.

examples.text: Cada habitación tiene su llave.
examples.trans: Each room has its own key.

meanings.note: Refers to clear cooking stock or broth made by simmering vegetables, herbs, or meat.

examples.text: Preparamos un caldo casero de verduras para la sopa de lentejas.
examples.trans: We made a homemade vegetable broth for the lentil soup.

examples.text: En invierno apetece mucho una taza de caldo bien caliente.
examples.trans: In winter a cup of piping hot broth really hits the spot.

meanings.note: Describes hot drinks, food, or water.

examples.text: Es una pieza caliente.
examples.trans: It is a hot piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene, señora: té caliente de menta con miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea with honey.

meanings.note: A foundational aromatic in Spanish cooking, sautéed slowly in olive oil until golden.

examples.text: Picamos una cebolla dulce muy fina para el sofrito.
examples.trans: We chopped a sweet onion very finely for the sauté base.

examples.text: La cebolla se dora despacio en la olla con aceite de oliva.
examples.trans: The onion browns slowly in the pot with olive oil.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ending in -dad.

examples.text: La ciudad está aquí.
examples.trans: The city is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ciudades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cities from the door.

meanings.note: Both the kitchen room and the stove/cuisine.

examples.text: La cocina está aquí.
examples.trans: The kitchen is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cocinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the kitchens from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; reflexive cocinarse is used when food cooks ('los dados se cocinan a la misma velocidad').

examples.text: Los domingos cocinamos todos juntos en la cocina grande.
examples.trans: On Sundays we all cook together in the big kitchen.

examples.text: Las lentejas se cocinan despacio a fuego muy suave.
examples.trans: The lentils cook slowly over very gentle heat.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Corto el pan en rebanadas finas.
examples.trans: I slice the bread into thin slices.

examples.text: La panadera cortó cuatro trozos de bizcocho.
examples.trans: The baker cut four pieces of sponge cake.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza crujiente.
examples.trans: It is a crispy piece.

examples.text: ¡Hornea muchas esquinas crujientes, cariño!
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, my dear!

meanings.note: Describes either an inquisitive person or an intriguing detail.

examples.text: Es una pieza curiosa.
examples.trans: It is a curious piece.

examples.text: ¡Qué curioso! La letra de esa etiqueta me resultaba muy familiar.
examples.trans: How curious! The handwriting on that tag felt very familiar to me.

meanings.note: Cortar en dados means 'to dice into neat cubes'.

examples.text: Corta las patatas y las zanahorias en dados pequeños.
examples.trans: Cut the potatoes and carrots into small cubes.

examples.text: Los dados de verdura se cuecen rápido en el caldo.
examples.trans: The diced vegetables cook quickly in the broth.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday single-word opposite of rápido.

examples.text: Camina despacio por las escaleras.
examples.trans: Walk slowly on the stairs.

examples.text: Gira la rueda muy despacio.
examples.trans: Turn the wheel very slowly.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb.

examples.text: Rara vez discutimos en el trabajo.
examples.trans: We rarely argue at work.

examples.text: Discutieron por una tontería antigua.
examples.trans: They argued over an old trifle.

meanings.note: Derived from oro ('gold'); in cooking, dorar means to sauté or bake until golden brown.

examples.text: Remueve la cebolla tres minutos hasta dorar en aceite de oliva.
examples.trans: Stir the onion for three minutes until golden in olive oil.

examples.text: Los bollos de canela se doraron enseguida en el horno caliente.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls turned golden brown quickly in the hot oven.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

echar.gloss: to pour; to toss; to miss (echar de menos)

meanings.en: to pour; to toss; to miss (echar de menos)
meanings.note: Echar un vistazo = take a glance; echar de menos = miss someone.

examples.text: Echa un poco más de agua caliente.
examples.trans: Pour a little more hot water.

examples.text: Te he echado mucho de menos.
examples.trans: I have missed you very much.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.text: Espere un momento, por favor.
examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.

examples.text: Esperamos que descanse muy bien.
examples.trans: We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.

examples.text: ¿Dónde están las llaves de latón?
examples.trans: Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: As a masculine noun (el final), means the ending of a song, book, or day.

examples.text: El final del vals baja el ritmo poco a poco.
examples.trans: The ending of the waltz slows the tempo little by little.

examples.text: Al final de la tarde probamos las dos sopas.
examples.trans: At the end of the afternoon we tasted both soups.

meanings.note: Pintura fresca = wet paint; agua fresca = cool water.

examples.text: Es una pieza fresca.
examples.trans: It is a cool piece.

examples.text: Bien. Pon estas hierbas frescas por encima antes de servirlos.
examples.trans: Good. Put these fresh herbs on top before serving them.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for the science of physics; as an adjective (físico/física), it means 'physical'.

examples.text: Cortar verduras del mismo tamaño para que se hagan a la vez es física básica.
examples.trans: Cutting vegetables the same size so they cook at once is basic physics.

examples.text: Su hermano estudió física y diseño acústico en la universidad.
examples.trans: His brother studied physics and acoustic design at university.

ganar.gloss: to win; to beat (ganar a); to earn

meanings.en: to win; to beat (ganar a); to earn
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Esta vista gana a cualquier postal.
examples.trans: This view beats any postcard.

examples.text: Con paciencia siempre ganamos tiempo.
examples.trans: With patience we always save time.

guardar.gloss: to keep; to put away; to guard

meanings.en: to keep; to put away; to guard
meanings.note: Everyday verb for putting something safely away in a pocket or cupboard.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en este cajón.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in this drawer.

examples.text: Te guardé el último rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I saved the last cinnamon roll for you.

hacer.gloss: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)

meanings.en: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)
meanings.note: Irregular: hago, hice, hecho; hace tres años = three years ago.

examples.text: La panadera hace pan fresco cada mañana.
examples.trans: The baker bakes fresh bread every morning.

examples.text: Llegó hace diez minutos.
examples.trans: She arrived ten minutes ago.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Hermano mayor = older brother; hermano pequeño = younger brother.

examples.text: El hermano está aquí.
examples.trans: The brother is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hermanos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the brothers from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing -ir verb (e -> ie in present: hierve, hierva; e -> i in 3rd preterite: hirvió).

examples.text: Cuando el agua empiece a hervir, apaga el fuego y prepara el té.
examples.trans: When the water starts to boil, turn off the heat and make the tea.

examples.text: La sopa de lentejas hierve despacio en la olla de barro.
examples.trans: The lentil soup simmers slowly in the clay pot.

meanings.note: Covers sewing thread, kitchen twine (hilo de cocina), and a thin stream of liquid (un hilo de aceite).

examples.text: Atamos las ramitas de tomillo y perejil con hilo de cocina.
examples.trans: We tied the sprigs of thyme and parsley with kitchen twine.

examples.text: Cose el botón suelto con aguja e hilo blanco.
examples.trans: Sew the loose button on with a needle and white thread.

meanings.note: Traditional large crusty round loaf of bread in Spain.

examples.text: Sacamos seis hogazas doradas y crujientes del horno.
examples.trans: We pulled six golden, crusty loaves from the oven.

examples.text: Corta rebanadas gruesas de la hogaza para la sopa.
examples.trans: Cut thick slices from the country loaf for the soup.

meanings.note: El día de hoy = today.

examples.text: Hoy es viernes por fin.
examples.trans: Today is finally Friday.

examples.text: ¿Qué desayunamos hoy?
examples.trans: What are we having for breakfast today?

meanings.note: Exact match in appearance.

examples.text: Es una pieza idéntica.
examples.trans: It is an identical piece.

examples.text: ¡Por fuera es idéntica, sí! ¡Pero mire por dentro!
examples.trans: On the outside it is identical, yes! Yet look on the inside!

meanings.note: Igual que = just like / the same as.

examples.text: Es una pieza igual.
examples.trans: It is a same piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Feminine form of jefe.

examples.text: En la cocina manda siempre nuestra jefa Rocío.
examples.trans: In the kitchen our head chef Rocio is always in charge.

examples.text: La jefa probó el caldo con una cuchara limpia.
examples.trans: The boss tasted the broth with a clean spoon.

meanings.note: Junto a + noun works like a preposition meaning 'beside / next to'.

examples.text: Siéntate junto a la ventana.
examples.trans: Sit next to the window.

examples.text: Trabajamos juntos en la posada.
examples.trans: We work together at the guesthouse.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Usually plural (lentejas) when referring to lentil soup or stew.

examples.text: Una sopa caliente de lentejas reconforta en invierno.
examples.trans: A hot lentil soup is comforting in winter.

examples.text: Cocemos las lentejas a fuego lento con verduras frescas.
examples.trans: We simmer the lentils slowly with fresh vegetables.

llamar.gloss: to call; to ring; to be named (llamarse)

meanings.en: to call; to ring; to be named (llamarse)
meanings.note: ¿Cómo se llama? asks someone's name.

examples.text: Soy de aquí, mucho gusto.
examples.trans: I am from here, pleased to meet you.

examples.text: Alguien llamó por teléfono ayer.
examples.trans: Someone called by phone yesterday.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.

examples.text: ¡Hasta luego, que tengas buen día!
examples.trans: See you later, have a good day!

meanings.note: Antepenultimate stress (esdrújula); tener lágrimas en los ojos = to have tears in one's eyes.

examples.text: Al oír el viejo vals, el vecino tenía lágrimas de emoción en los ojos.
examples.trans: On hearing the old waltz, the neighbour had tears of emotion in his eyes.

examples.text: Cortar cebolla siempre me saca alguna lágrima.
examples.trans: Chopping onions always brings a tear to my eye.

meanings.note: Built from mano ('hand'); in the kitchen, las manoplas are padded oven mitts.

examples.text: Ponte las manoplas gruesas antes de sacar la bandeja del horno.
examples.trans: Put on the thick oven mitts before taking the tray out of the oven.

examples.text: Colgó las manoplas de tela junto a los delantales.
examples.trans: He hung the cloth oven mitts next to the aprons.

meanings.note: Irregular comparative/superlative of bueno; plural mejores.

examples.text: Esta ventana tiene la mejor vista.
examples.trans: This window has the best view.

examples.text: Hoy el radiador calienta mejor.
examples.trans: Today the radiator heats better.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.text: Mi maleta es azul marino.
examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: En cinco minutos = in five minutes.

examples.text: El minuto está aquí.
examples.trans: The minute is here.

examples.text: Vemos los minutos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the minutes from the door.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.text: Tenemos el mismo trabajo.
examples.trans: We have the same job.

examples.text: Ahora mismo estoy ocupada.
examples.trans: I am busy right now.

meanings.note: Accented más means 'more / most'; de más = extra.

examples.text: ¿Quiere un poco más de té?
examples.trans: Would you like a little more tea?

examples.text: Es la habitación más tranquila.
examples.trans: It is the quietest room.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Necesito un bolígrafo para firmar.
examples.trans: I need a pen to sign.

examples.text: ¿Necesitan ustedes alguna toalla más?
examples.trans: Do you all need another towel?

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.text: Hoy no llueve en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

nos.gloss: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)

meanings.en: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)
meanings.note: First-person plural object/reflexive/reciprocal pronoun.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos mañana por la mañana!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow morning!

examples.text: Nos alegra mucho la noticia.
examples.trans: The news makes us very glad.

meanings.note: Precede the verb alone (nunca llega tarde) or follow no.

examples.text: Nunca he visto ese cofre antes.
examples.trans: I have never seen that chest before.

examples.text: El tren de la mañana nunca llega tarde.
examples.trans: The morning train never arrives late.

meanings.note: Las ocho = eight o'clock.

examples.text: Abrimos la puerta a las ocho.
examples.trans: We open the door at eight.

examples.text: La posada tiene ocho habitaciones.
examples.trans: The guesthouse has eight rooms.

meanings.note: In Valencia and eastern Spain, oliva is used alongside aceituna for the olive fruit.

examples.text: Un chorrito de aceite de oliva realza las lentejas.
examples.trans: A drizzle of olive oil brings out the lentils.

examples.text: Traemos aceite de oliva virgen del mercado local.
examples.trans: We bring virgin olive oil from the local market.

meanings.note: Standard word for a deep cooking pot with two handles used for soups, stews, and broths.

examples.text: La olla grande ya está al fuego con un chorrito de aceite de oliva.
examples.trans: The big pot is already on the stove with a drizzle of olive oil.

examples.text: Destapó la olla y toda la cocina olió a tomillo y verduras.
examples.trans: He lifted the lid off the pot and the whole kitchen smelled of thyme and vegetables.

meanings.note: Irregular: oigo, oyes, oye, oímos, oís, oyen; ¡Oiga! / ¡Oye! gets someone's attention.

examples.text: ¿Me oyes bien por teléfono?
examples.trans: Can you hear me clearly on the phone?

examples.text: Acabo de oír pasos en la escalera.
examples.trans: I just heard footsteps on the stairs.

meanings.note: Plural los panes; pan recién hecho = freshly baked bread.

examples.text: El pan es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The bread is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el pan.
examples.trans: We talk about the bread.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.text: El patio está aquí.
examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: One of the most widely used fresh green herbs in Spanish home cooking.

examples.text: Cortamos unas hojas de perejil fresco de la maceta del patio.
examples.trans: We snipped a few leaves of fresh parsley from the courtyard pot.

examples.text: Un poco de perejil picado da mucho color y aroma a la sopa.
examples.trans: A little chopped parsley gives great colour and aroma to the soup.

meanings.note: De piedra = made of stone.

examples.text: La piedra está aquí.
examples.trans: The stone is here.

examples.text: Vemos las piedras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stones from the door.

meanings.note: Una pizca de sal is the standard cooking measure for a tiny pinch.

examples.text: Añade una pizca de sal fina a la masa dulce.
examples.trans: Add a pinch of fine salt to the sweet pastry.

examples.text: Probamos una pizca de crema con una cuchara limpia.
examples.trans: We taste a tiny dab of cream with a clean spoon.

poner.gloss: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)

meanings.en: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)
meanings.note: Irregular: pongo, pon, puse, puesto; ponerse nervioso = get nervous.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas limpias en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two clean cups on the table.

examples.text: Pon la maleta junto al mostrador.
examples.trans: Set the suitcase beside the counter.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Sin querer = by accident; querer decir = to mean.

examples.text: ¿Quiere usted café o té caliente?
examples.trans: Would you like coffee or hot tea?

examples.text: Lo abrí sin querer.
examples.trans: I opened it by accident.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.text: ¿Qué hora es ahora mismo?
examples.trans: What time is it right now?

examples.text: ¡Qué mañana tan luminosa!
examples.trans: What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Diminutive of rama ('branch'); standard culinary word for a sprig of herbs (una ramita de tomillo o romero).

examples.text: Pon dos ramitas de tomillo fresco dentro de la olla.
examples.trans: Put two sprigs of fresh thyme inside the pot.

examples.text: Decoró la jarra de limonada con una ramita de menta.
examples.trans: She garnished the pitcher of lemonade with a sprig of mint.

meanings.note: Pan recién hecho = freshly baked bread; recién salido del horno = fresh out of the oven.

examples.text: Tenemos pan recién hecho cada día.
examples.trans: We have freshly baked bread every day.

examples.text: El zumo está recién exprimido.
examples.trans: The juice is freshly squeezed.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: recuerdo).

examples.text: Recuerdo perfectamente aquella tarde.
examples.trans: I remember that afternoon perfectly.

examples.text: ¿Recuerdas dónde guardamos el plano?
examples.trans: Do you remember where we put the blueprint?

meanings.note: Covers wristwatches, wall clocks, and church tower clocks (plural: relojes).

examples.text: El reloj está aquí.
examples.trans: The watch is here.

examples.text: Vemos los relojes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the watchs from the door.

meanings.note: In Peninsular Spanish, remover means 'to stir' (paint, soup, or coffee); stem-changing o -> ue.

examples.text: Remueve bien la pintura del fondo antes de empezar.
examples.trans: Stir the paint up from the bottom thoroughly before starting.

examples.text: Rocío remueve despacio las lentejas con cuchara de palo.
examples.trans: Rocio stirs the lentils slowly with a wooden spoon.

examples.text: Para todo. Desde luego me gusta un montón y hace reír.
examples.trans: For everything. I definitely like him a lot and he makes people laugh.

examples.text: Hablamos de reír en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about to laugh at the office.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number.

examples.text: Es una pieza roja.
examples.trans: It is a red piece.

examples.text: ¡Dígales que la mía tiene una cinta roja en el bolsillo de arriba!
examples.trans: Tell them mine has a red ribbon in the top pocket!

meanings.note: Con sal = salted; sin sal = unsalted.

examples.text: La sal es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The salt is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la sal.
examples.trans: We talk about the salt.

salir.gloss: to go out; to come out; to leave

meanings.en: to go out; to come out; to leave
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg salgo; salir corriendo = run out.

examples.text: El pan acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The bread just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Salgo temprano hacia la estación.
examples.trans: I leave early for the station.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suena).

examples.text: El despertador suena a las seis y media.
examples.trans: The alarm clock rings at six thirty.

examples.text: El piano sonaba cálido bajo la lluvia.
examples.trans: The piano sounded warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Hecho una sopa = soaked through.

examples.text: La sopa está aquí.
examples.trans: The soup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las sopas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the soups from the door.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.text: Sí, la habitación está lista.
examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.

examples.text: ¡Claro que sí, pase usted!
examples.trans: Of course, come right in!

meanings.note: Tablas de madera = wooden planks.

examples.text: La tabla está aquí.
examples.trans: The plank is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tablas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the planks from the door.

meanings.note: Por teléfono = by phone / on the phone.

examples.text: El teléfono está aquí.
examples.trans: The telephone is here.

examples.text: Vemos los teléfonos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the telephones from the door.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Classic Mediterranean herb that grows wild on sunny hillsides and in courtyard pots.

examples.text: El tomillo fresco da un aroma de campo maravilloso a las lentejas.
examples.trans: Fresh thyme gives a wonderful country aroma to the lentils.

examples.text: Plantamos tomillo, romero y menta junto al muro del jardín.
examples.trans: We planted thyme, rosemary, and mint beside the garden wall.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ponemos tres mesas bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We set three tables under the tree.

examples.text: Empieza con tres frases cortas.
examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.

meanings.note: El tráfico del centro = city-centre traffic.

examples.text: El tráfico es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The traffic is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el tráfico.
examples.trans: We talk about the traffic.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: A la misma velocidad = 'at the same speed / rate'; a toda velocidad = 'at top speed'.

examples.text: Los dados iguales de zanahoria se cocinan a la misma velocidad.
examples.trans: Equal-sized carrot cubes cook at the exact same speed.

examples.text: El tren regional cruzó el valle a buena velocidad.
examples.trans: The regional train crossed the valley at a good speed.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos luego en el patio!
examples.trans: See you later in the courtyard!

meanings.note: Sopa de verduras = vegetable soup.

examples.text: La verdura está aquí.
examples.trans: The vegetable is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verduras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the vegetables from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: ¡Ya está! = All done!; ya no = no longer.

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is already ready.

examples.text: ¡Ya voy con las llaves!
examples.trans: Coming right now with the keys!

meanings.note: Silent medial -h-; pronounced [θanaˈoɾja] in Peninsular Spanish.

examples.text: Pela seis zanahorias frescas para la sopa de lentejas.
examples.trans: Peel six fresh carrots for the lentil soup.

examples.text: Cortamos la zanahoria en dados iguales sobre la tabla.
examples.trans: We dice the carrot into even cubes on the board.
